title: Hyperspectral Imaging (TIVITA) for Determining the Optimal Timing of Pedicle Division in Pedicled Supraclavicular Island Flaps: A Prospective Observational Study
summary: Sometimes a larger wound on the head or neck must be closed using a piece of skin taken from the shoulder. To ensure this piece of skin receives enough blood at first, it initially remains connected to the shoulder by a strip of tissue. Only once the skin has grown in well at its new location is this connecting strip separated, in a second, smaller operation. Until now, doctors have mainly relied on clinical experience to judge the right time for this second operation. This study investigates whether a special camera can instead measure this timing objectively. The camera measures, from a distance and without any contact or radiation, how well the transplanted skin is supplied with blood. The aim is to avoid unnecessary waiting time and make the treatment safer.
conditions: Defects in the head and neck region requiring reconstruction with a pedicled supraclavicular island flap (e.g. following tumour resection, scar contractures, or orocutaneous fistulas), regardless of the underlying diagnosis.

interventions.name: Patients receiving a pedicled supraclavicular island flap for the reconstruction of a defect in the head and neck region. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient undergoing reconstruction of a head and neck defect with a pedicled supraclavicular island flap, regardless of the underlying diagnosis.
The patient agrees to participate after study-specific information has been provided and is able to comply with all study-related requirements (e.g. attendance at follow-up appointments).
Exclusion criteria:
Minors and patients lacking capacity to consent.
Severe systemic diseases affecting wound healing.
